answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer, any disruption from an untested primary-vendor switch carries outsized delivery risk—exactly what the objective warns against. Memory_c2 supports switching but is the single most consequential and least-corroborated claim (only one record, no mention of sustained performance or risk under tight capacity), so it's the one worth verifying before ruling anything out. Meanwhile memory_c4 and memory_c6 both show renegotiation with the incumbent can materially cut unit cost or unlock volume pricing without touching integration stability (memory_c1), which directly serves the cost mandate while holding delivery risk flat. This is a smaller, reversible move that keeps the higher-risk vendor switch as a live option for next cycle once verified, rather than committing capacity to an unproven low-cost transition during a zero-slack production period.
